Exercise B

Reading: Cooking Stations & Kitchen Rules

Read the texts below, then answer the questions — just like Reading Parts 1 and 2 in the real MSA exam.

Part 1 — Match the Student to the Cooking Station

Smoothie Station: Blend fresh fruit and yoghurt into a healthy cold drink in seconds.

Salad Bar: Mix crunchy vegetables with a simple dressing for a colourful, fresh lunch.

Soup Pot: Learn to make a warming vegetable soup from cheap, everyday ingredients.

Snack Table: Prepare quick, healthy snacks such as fruit skewers and vegetable dips.

Exercise C

Writing: Blog Post

Choose ONE of the two prompts below and write 80–100 words, just like Writing Part 3 in the real MSA exam. This section is graded by your teacher, not automatically.

Choose ONE prompt

Prompt 1: Write a blog post describing the healthy-eating workshop. What did you make, and what did you learn?

Prompt 2: Do you think schools should teach students how to cook and eat healthily? Give your opinion and reasons.
